question_text: A shell is fired vertically upward with a velocity $20\text{ m/s}$ from a trolley moving horizontally with velocity $10\text{ m/s}$. A person on the ground observes the motion of the shell to be like a parabola whose horizontal range is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
solution:
From the frame of reference of a person on the ground:
- Horizontal component of velocity of the shell: $u_x = 10\text{ m/s}$
- Vertical component of velocity of the shell: $u_y = 20\text{ m/s}$

The time of flight $T$ is determined by the vertical motion:
$$T = \frac{2 u_y}{g} = \frac{2 \times 20}{10} = 4\text{ s}$$

The horizontal range $R$ observed from the ground is:
$$R = u_x \times T = 10\text{ m/s} \times 4\text{ s} = 40\text{ m}$$

Hence, the correct option is (3).

question_text: A particle is moving along a circular path of radius $a$ with constant angular velocity $\omega$. Magnitude of displacement of the particle as a function of time $t$ is
solution:
In time $t$, the angular displacement of the particle is $\theta = \omega t$.

The magnitude of the displacement vector $|\Delta \vec{r}|$ for a particle moving on a circle of radius $a$ through an angle $\theta$ is given by the chord length:
$$|\Delta \vec{r}| = 2a \sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)$$

Substituting $\theta = \omega t$:
$$|\Delta \vec{r}| = 2a \sin\left(\frac{\omega t}{2}\right)$$

Hence, the correct option is (4).

question_text: Time of flight of a body dropped from a height is $T$. If another body is projected horizontally with speed $v$ from the same height, then its time of flight will be
solution:
The vertical motion and horizontal motion of a projectile are independent of each other.

For a freely dropped body from height $h$ with initial vertical velocity $u_y = 0$:
$$h = \frac{1}{2}g T^2 \implies T = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}$$

For a body projected horizontally with speed $v$, its initial vertical velocity is also $u_y = 0$. Therefore, the time taken to hit the ground depends solely on the vertical motion:
$$t = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} = T$$

Thus, the time of flight remains unchanged at $T$.

Hence, the correct option is (1).

question_text: In the given diagram shown for a projectile, what is the angle of projection?
diagram_description: A graph showing the parabolic path of a projectile launched from the origin $(0,0)$ at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. A point on the trajectory has a vertical height of $20\text{ m}$. The horizontal distance from the origin to the projection of this point on the x-axis is $30\text{ m}$, and the remaining horizontal distance from this point to the point of landing on the x-axis is $10\text{ m}$.
solution:
From the given figure:
- Total horizontal range $R = 30\text{ m} + 10\text{ m} = 40\text{ m}$
- A point on the trajectory is $(x, y) = (30\text{ m}, 20\text{ m})$

The trajectory equation of a projectile in terms of horizontal range $R$ is:
$$y = x \tan\theta \left(1 - \frac{x}{R}\right)$$

Substituting $x = 30$, $y = 20$, and $R = 40$:
$$20 = 30 \tan\theta \left(1 - \frac{30}{40}\right)$$
$$20 = 30 \tan\theta \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)$$
$$20 = \frac{15}{2} \tan\theta$$
$$\tan\theta = \frac{20 \times 2}{15} = \frac{40}{15} = \frac{8}{3}$$
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)$$

Hence, the correct option is (2).
